'''Eleventh Meghalaya Assembly''' constituted after the [[2023 Meghalaya Legislative Assembly election]]. Elections were held in [[List of constituencies of the Meghalaya Legislative Assembly|59]] constituencies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Singharia |first=Kanishka |date=2023-01-18 |title=Meghalaya polls to be held on Feb 27, results on March 2 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/meghalaya-polls-to-be-held-on-feb-27-results-on-march-2-101674034750467.html |access-date=2023-03-02 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> Voting on [[Sohiong Assembly constituency|Sohiong]] was postponed after the death of UDP's candidate H. D. R. Lyngdoh.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ANI |date=2023-02-21 |title=Polling postponed in Sohiong, Meghalaya after UDP candidate's death |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/elections/polling-postponed-in-sohiong-meghalaya-after-udp-candidate-s-death-123022100374_1.html |access-date=2023-03-02 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
After results were declared on 2 March 2023, it resulted into a hung assembly. Ruling NPP got 26 seats however BJP supported [[Meghalaya Democratic Alliance (2018)|MDA]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-02 |title=Meghalaya Election Results 2023 highlights: BJP submits letter of support to NPP |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/meghalaya-election-result-2023-live-60-assembly-constituencies-election-news-101677714304477.html |access-date=2023-03-02 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Anamni |last2=Suresh |first2=Anandu |date=2023-03-02 |title=Meghalaya Election Results 2023 Live Updates: Conrad Sangma falls short of majority, dials Amit Shah for BJP support to form govt |url=https://indianexpress.com/elections/meghalaya-election-result-2023-live-updates-assembly-election-vote-counting-today-bjp-congress-cpi-latest-news-8473285/ |access-date=2023-03-02 |website=[[The Indian Express]] |language=en}}</ref>
